data.narrative:
Varda Space Industries, a Series D-stage space technology company founded by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov, is evaluated against a comparable universe of five public Space & Aerospace companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private peers including Impulse Space, Apex Space, and others at similar or adjacent stages. The target has raised $329M to date against a current post-money valuation of $1.58B.

Two quantitative methods apply to this valuation. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $1.5B last post-money and applying a typical 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier, implies $2.2B. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector comparables—Sierra Space ($8.0B, Series C), Impulse Space ($4.3B, Series D), Apex Space ($2.3B, Series D), and Skyryse ($1.1B, Series C)—yields a median valuation of $3.3B, with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied; the median P/S multiple for the sector is 24.6x across six traded companies, but Varda's revenue is not on file, precluding multiples-based inference.

Triangulating these two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $1.9B (low) to $3.8B (high), with a median estimate of $2.8B. Key uncertainties include execution risk specific to orbital manufacturing operations, capital intensity of scaling, and wide dispersion in peer valuations reflecting stage and market conditions. The current $1.58B valuation sits below the low-end triangulated estimate.
